title: Boss: it works on my machine
summary: Diagnose connectivity tickets and plan an rsync deploy.

steps.title: Support queue
steps.body: The deploy pipeline uses rsync over ssh, and three tickets are about connectivity. Model the tools to answer them.

steps.title: Triage the symptom
prompt: Write `string Diagnose(string curlError, bool listensOnAllInterfaces)` mapping what `curl` reported to the layer to investigate:
- contains `Connection refused` → `"bind"` if not `listensOnAllInterfaces`, else `"not running"`
hints: A chain of `if` statements in the listed order.
Refused with a loopback-only listener is a bind problem.
template: Dojo.Eq("dns", "dns", Diagnose("curl: (6) Could not resolve host: api.internal", true));
Dojo.Eq("firewall", "firewall", Diagnose("curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.0.0.5 port 443 after 30001 ms: Connection timed out", true));
Dojo.Eq("bind", "bind", Diagnose("curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.0.0.5 port 5000: Connection refused", false));
Dojo.Eq("not running", "not running", Diagnose("curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.0.0.5 port 5000: Connection refused", true));

steps.title: Plan an rsync
prompt: Write `List<string> RsyncPlan(Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> src, Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> dst, bool delete)` returning what `rsync -a` (quick check mode) would do, sorted by path (ordinal):
- path only in `src`, or in both but size **or** mtime differ → `"send <path>"`,
- path only in `dst` → `"delete <path>"` only when `delete` is true,
starter: List<string> RsyncPlan(Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> src, Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> dst, bool delete)
solution: List<string> RsyncPlan(Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> src, Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> dst, bool delete)
var plan = new List<(string Path, string Line)>();
if (!dst.TryGetValue(path, out var d) || d != meta) plan.Add((path, $"send {path}"));
hints: Collect (path, line) pairs, then sort by path at the end.
template: var dojoSrc = new Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> { ["app.dll"] = (900, 200), ["appsettings.json"] = (40, 100), ["new.dll"] = (10, 300) };
var dojoDst = new Dictionary<string, (long Size, long Mtime)> { ["app.dll"] = (880, 150), ["appsettings.json"] = (40, 100), ["old.dll"] = (5, 50) };
Dojo.Eq("no --delete", new List<string> { "send app.dll", "send new.dll" }, RsyncPlan(dojoSrc, dojoDst, false));
Dojo.Eq("with --delete", new List<string> { "send app.dll", "send new.dll", "delete old.dll" }, RsyncPlan(dojoSrc, dojoDst, true));

steps.title: Ping summary
prompt: After the deploy, a health job pings every host. Write `string PingSummary(List<double?> rtts)` where each entry is one reply's round-trip time in ms, or `null` for a lost packet. Return the same summary lines ping prints, joined by `\n`:
Loss is a whole percentage (rounded down). Times use 3 decimals. If nothing was received, return only the first line.
solution: string first = $"{rtts.Count} packets transmitted, {got.Count} received, {loss}% packet loss";
hints: Integer division rounds down for you.
template: Dojo.Eq("some loss", "4 packets transmitted, 3 received, 25% packet loss\nrtt min/avg/max = 10.000/20.000/30.000 ms", PingSummary(new List<double?> { 10, null, 20, 30 }));
Dojo.Eq("rounding down", "3 packets transmitted, 2 received, 33% packet loss\nrtt min/avg/max = 1.500/2.250/3.000 ms", PingSummary(new List<double?> { 1.5, 3, null }));
Dojo.Eq("all lost", "2 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss", PingSummary(new List<double?> { null, null }));
